One pulse of 18, 34, 50... ticks every time the input turns on, even for the shortest input (2 ticks): a copper bulb notices the rising edge, a second bulb holds the pulse and a loop of repeaters switches it off. Detail: extendable family oneshot-bulb-rise (n = 0): rising-edge with L = 18 + 16n gt, 19 + 4n blocks. the input toggles a copper bulb on every rising edge (even the shortest), a comparator reads it and an observer watching that comparator fires once per rising edge into a second bulb; a comparator reads the second bulb into a U of delay-4 repeaters back into it, which turns it off one loop later. Extension: lengthen the repeater U by one row: one more delay-4 repeater (on stone) in each column. Generator: mctas circuit pulse family oneshot-bulb-rise --n N --out FILE.

One 10-tick pulse (half a second) every time the input turns on AND every time it turns off, from just 2 blocks, for quiet builds: the input opens and closes a trapdoor, and a sound sensor (calibrated sculk sensor) switches on for 10 ticks at each sound. Detail: block_open (10) and block_close (9); nothing at the sensor's back: every frequency.

One 10-tick pulse every time the input turns on and every time it turns off, from 3 blocks, for quiet builds, handling inputs from 15 ticks (half the 2-block version's 30): the input opens and closes a trapdoor; one sound sensor hears every sound it is free for, and a second one, whose back touches the input, listens only while the input is off, so it catches the closing even while the first one is still resting. Detail: calibrated sculk sensors; block_open (10), block_close (9); the input's 15 at the second sensor's back accepts only 15.

Stretches any input, even the shortest input (2 ticks), into exactly 10 ticks (half a second), from just 2 blocks, for quiet builds: the input makes a note block play, and a sound sensor (calibrated sculk sensor) that hears it switches on for exactly 10 ticks. Stretches any input, even the shortest input (2 ticks), into exactly 10 ticks (half a second), and footsteps or dropped items nearby never set it off: the input makes a note block play, a calibrated sculk sensor (a sound sensor) hears it and switches on for exactly 10 ticks however short or long the input was, and a comparator reading a chest tunes the sensor to that one kind of sound.
